summary: 72-foot steel lookout with wooden cab, built 1949 on Taum Sauk, Missouri's highest point; inside Taum Sauk Mountain State Park; NHLR-registered April 1997.

facts.design: 72-foot steel tower with wooden cab; a 1950 press report gives a ten by ten cab

access.note: The tower stands inside Taum Sauk Mountain State Park, which the state invites visitors to climb. No closure notice was found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: A paved trail runs to the highpoint. A 2025 blog visitor climbed the tower.

events.note: Constructed in 1949 (Register); steel structure still being erected in July 1949 after weather and road delays
Temporary towerman Sam Jones reported in March 1950; he planned to ride a mare to the tower because no road was finished
Access road finished in FY 1951-52; dedication set for October 1952, sponsored by the Arcadia Valley Rotary Club
Tower cab received a new roof and siding in FY 1966-67
Road constructed at the tower site in FY 1975-76
Taum Sauk Mountain State Park created by Missouri

corrections.why: The Register gives the tower as 72 feet (about 21.9 m). No source supports 235.3 m, which would be about 772 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 85 feet (July 1949, during erection), 60 feet (November 1950 press report), and 72 feet (the Register and a 2025 blog). The facts use 72 feet (21.9 m) from the Register. The story gives the other figures.
The Register says steel tower with wooden cab. A 1953 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts calls the tower all-steel. The facts follow the Register.

sources.title: An early "March" up two fire lookouts in Missouri

notes_for_editor: Most of the history (1948-1981) comes from newspaper and annual-report extracts transcribed on Forest Lookouts; the quotes were checked against that cached page, not the original papers. No fire events are named in any source read, so none are stated. Height disagrees across sources (60, 72 and 85 ft); facts use the Register's 72 ft. The brief's height_m of 235.3 is unsupported and is corrected. Access: no closure notice found; the state park page does not mention the tower, so public access rests on park status and the 2025 blog visit. The Wikidata entry lists the Missouri Department of Conservation as operator and names a Commons photo, 'View from Taum Sauk Mountain Lookout Tower.JPG', which was not checked for licence and is not added. Nothing after the 1980s is documented apart from the 1991 park, the 1997 registration and the 2025 visit.
